ain-Latn.original_value: Commons or ta noka oruspe a=kopisi eaykap.
ain-Latn.reviewed_followup_value: Tatum (noka oruspe) anak Commons a=konu eaykap.
ain-Latn.value: Tatum (noka oruspe) anak Commons a=konu eaykap.
ain-Latn.backtranslation: As for the data (information concerning the image), one could not inquire of Commons about it.
ain-Latn.ui_backtranslation: Could not query Commons for the image information.
ain-Latn.confidence: medium for semantic and grammatical adequacy; low-to-medium for idiomatic naturalness
ain-Latn.rationale: The replacement resolves the original valency objection: konu licenses an addressee/source and queried content. The content is raised with anak, leaving Commons as the unmarked addressee, rather than using locative or ta. The indefinite transitive a= and post-verbal eaykap construction are independently supported by Tamura’s grammar. Tatum identifies computing data and the parenthesis specifies image-related information, so the whole clause expresses failed inquiry for descriptive data rather than image retrieval. Acceptance is a contextual compositional judgment, not inferred from dictionary words alone.
ain-Latn.metadata_scope: Contextual image-attribution metadata paraphrase, including descriptive/rights information; no missing-data assertion.

mn-Mong.backtranslation: The request to query Commons for information about the picture did not succeed.
mn-Mong.transliteration: Commons-ača ǰiruγ-un medegelel-i lablaqu küselte bütügsen ügei.
mn-Mong.confidence: medium contextual grammatical and semantic adequacy
mn-Mong.rationale: The sentence explicitly makes the inquiry request its subject. Commons-ača identifies the information source, picture-GEN and information-ACC specify the requested material, and lablaqu modifies the request noun. The nominal request prevents the broad inquire/check stem from standing alone as metadata validation. The past verbal noun bütügsen followed by independent ügei states non-accomplishment, supported by the primary morphology study. Traditional-script lexical forms were checked directly against the dictionary, rather than produced by automatic Cyrillic substitution.
mn-Mong.script_convention: Traditional Mongolian Unicode letters; back-vowel source suffix ača for the ordinary back-vowel pronunciation of Commons; un after ǰiruγ and i after consonant-final medegelel. U+1803 full stop. Three U+202F separated-suffix connectors are retained as a Unicode-supported legacy convention.

ryu.romanization: Commons nkai metadēta tanumushi nu naihanchan.
ryu.confidence: medium source-assisted contextual grammatical and semantic adequacy; not native-certified
ryu.rationale: The explicit addressee and transitive request clause resolve the earlier examination/lookup ambiguity. Primary dictionary evidence establishes the request verb, nominalizer, addressee case, inanimate subject marker and unsuccessful-completion predicate. An independently retrieved primary m-type paradigm supports the regular tanumu-shi formation; actual recorded speech attests nkai with the same request verb. A close primary request construction corroborates bare request-content syntax. Taken together these support the complete compositional sentence, not merely isolated translated words.

construction_checks.basis: NINJAL p435 addressee marker plus visually verified Arts p94 same request verb with nkai-marked teacher; software-service addressee is a bounded contextual extension.

Transparent technical object; no separate standardized Okinawan metadata term or whole Japanese sentence is claimed. Bare requested content has a close primary example with the unigē sun request construction.

NINJAL tanu=nuN has negative =maN and conjunctive =di; the m-type grammar table explicitly has short stem kamu- and nominalization kamu-ɕi. Applying that regular pattern produces tanumu-shi. No primary exact tanumu-shi token is claimed.
The dictionary permits nominative nu with inanimate subjects and supplies work plus nu with the failure predicate; the nominalized request is an abstract event subject.
NINJAL p405 explicitly gives the unsuccessful work sense; Miyara p219 independently indexed exact past form hanchan.

ryu.script_convention: Okinawan Kana with the preserved Latin Commons proper name, transparent Katakana metadata borrowing and U+3002 punctuation. Spacing is a readable modern UI convention; not a pan-Okinawan orthographic standard claim.
